extract.name: Full-Head Ejection System
extract.notes: Designed as an integral part of a 'Mech's head, taking up no more room than a standard Ejection Seat. The system is closely tied to standard life support equipment and any critical damage will trap the MechWarrior in the 'Mech. The MechWarrior is jolted around significantly during activation, increasing risk of concussions, contusions, and broken limbs. Later versions overcome the limitation of requiring the torso to be upright for ejection.

extract.name: Enhanced Imaging
extract.notes: Developed by the Clans, Enhanced Imaging is an advanced targeting and piloting system for use with humanoid-shaped combat vehicles such as BattleMechs, battle armor, and ProtoMechs. It combines an Enhanced Imaging Display and Enhanced Imaging Neural Implants. The system offers considerable advantages but inflicts serious side effects on the user, including possible mental instability, nerve damage and death. EI is the only viable control method for ProtoMechs. About 5 percent of all Clan warriors choose to receive the implants due to their dangerous and painful side effects. The system was used by Clan Smoke Jaguar in developing ProtoMechs, eliminating the need for a mechanical balancing system and allowing for a smaller cockpit. EI technology also has potential medicinal benefits for people with degenerative conditions like multiple sclerosis and muscular dystrophy.

extract.name: Direct Neural Interface
extract.notes: Proposed by Professor Burke Kale in 3043. Required brain surgery to install an interface port and required the MechWarrior to take compound XA-3 to protect the brain from dangerous feedback. Any damage taken during battle was much more likely to injure the pilot. The Federated Commonwealth decided not to pursue the project. The only known user was Burke Kale, who installed the DNI input jack in his brain in 3053. Kale stole the technology from the NAIS Dark Mirage facility on Hyde and went to Solaris, where he used a DNI-retrofitted Prometheus 'Mech. He later completed the Epimetheus 'Mech specifically designed for the DNI interface. The system was eventually copied by a ComStar ROM operative. Later used as basis for Manei Domini's Vehicular Direct Neural Interface and Clan ProtoMech Enhanced Imaging system.

extract.name: Remote Drone Operating System
extract.notes: Unlike more sophisticated autonomous robotic drones, a Remote Drone Operating System requires human control of the unit which equips it. This remote control system has a limited range on planetary surfaces of about 80km (unless supplemented by satellites), while aerospace-based control systems have a range of 3,000,000km. A unit mounting the Remote Drone Operating System must be paired with a controller console such as the Drone Carrier Control System (Remote) which will provide the controlled unit with guidance. If the drone exceeds the control range, or if hostile ECM interferes with the signal, the controlled drone becomes immobile and inactive. The mass of the system is 10% of the equipped unit's mass, plus 0.5 tons for additional communications equipment. Remote Drones incur additional penalties on piloting checks and indirect fire, spotting, and fire while spotting.

extract.name: Drone Carrier Control System (Remote)
extract.notes: Unlike more sophisticated autonomous robotic drones, a remote Drone CCS requires human control of the units which it commands. This remote control system has a limited range on planetary surfaces of about 80km (unless supplemented by satellites), while aerospace-based control systems have a range of 3,000,000km. A vehicle or aerospace unit mounting the Carrier Control System may control any number of drone units of various types (e.g. a DropShip may control a mix of Drone ASF and Drone Battlemechs) and may mount as many CCS components as their construction rules allow. Each controlled unit must mount a Remote Drone Operating System. If a drone exceeds the control range, or if hostile ECM interferes with the signal, the controlled drone becomes immobile and inactive. The tonnage of each CCS component accounts for the crew stations needed to control the drone units (1 crew per drone) as well as additional communication equipment necessary for connecting to the controlled drones.

extract.name: Recon Camera
extract.notes: A Recon Camera has a maximum range of eighteen kilometers and can only be used on the Low Altitude map or ground map. Units equipped with a Recon Camera may act as a spotter for LRM Indirect Fire as if it were a TAG, but cannot use it to designate targets for other TAG-guided weapons, such as semi-guided LRMs, laser-guided bombs and Arrow IV artillery missiles. Hidden units that are passed over by a Recon Camera-equipped flier must reveal themselves on an unsuccessful 2d6 roll.

extract.name: Sprayer
extract.notes: Found most often on firefighting gear, Coolant Trucks, police riot control vehicles, and agricultural vehicles. A Sprayer is simply a hose and pump system that sprays liquids at a target. Though useful in commercial and nonmilitary applications, the Sprayer isn't as effective as the Fluid Gun on the battlefield due to its limited pumping power (which reduces range) and the ineffectiveness of the various sprayed fluids against armored targets. The Sprayer is usually found on IndustrialMechs and vehicles with internal Liquid Storage tanks. A Sprayer system can typically pump 10 kilograms of fluid per second. The Sprayer also gave birth to the Light Fluid Suction System, which is essentially a Sprayer with the hoses reversed so it sucks fluids into storage tanks. The Sprayer and Light Fluid Suction System can be used by any unit except BattleMechs and ProtoMechs. Sprayers may not gain any benefit from targeting computers or other fire control equipment, so they always have a +2 to hit penalty. They only affect conventional infantry units, acting as a battle armor flamer with a range of 1 hex. To operate the Sprayer or Light Fluid Suction system the engine of the carrying vehicle must be active, and the crew must be awake. A unit mounting a Sprayer or Suction System must devote tonnage to Liquid Storage. Support vehicle versions of these systems weigh 15 kg. They aren't counted as weapons and so don't require gunners.

extract.name: Buzzsaw
extract.notes: Special Rules for the Buzzsaw can be found on 'Unbound' pages 64 and 70. The Buzzsaw was likely replaced by the Chainsaw and Dual Saw in 'TechManual'.

extract.name: Light Fluid Suction System
extract.notes: Can be used by any unit except BattleMechs and ProtoMechs. May not gain any benefit from targeting computers or other fire control equipment, so they always have a +2 to hit penalty. They only affect conventional infantry units, acting as a battle armor flamer with a range of 1 hex. To operate the system the engine of the carrying vehicle must be active, and the crew must be awake. A unit mounting a Sprayer or Suction System must devote tonnage to Liquid Storage. When mounted on an IndustrialMech, a Sprayer/Suction System weighs 0.5 tons; Support vehicle versions of these systems weigh 15 kg. They aren't counted as weapons and so don't require gunners.

extract.name: Project Jacob's Ladder
extract.notes: The Delta Green security level for Project Jacob's Ladder is likely a reference to Delta Green, a line of Call of Cthulhu sourcebooks when Jacob's Ladder was introduced in the early 2000s.

extract.name: Vehicular Direct Neural Interface
extract.notes: In CBT play VDNI units receive a -1 modifier for all Gunnery and Piloting rolls. Unless the warrior is also equipped with a pain shunt, any internal structure damage and critical hits requires a roll of 2D6, with the warrior suffering 1 point of damage on a result of 8 or more. VDNI-equipped vehicles require only one pilot to operate and use the MechWarrior Consciousness Table to track damage to the pilot, while any Commander Hit, Gunner Hit and Crew Stunned results are treated as pilot hits. In RPG play, a VDNI-implanted operative with the requisite skills and plugged into a machine equipped to interface receives +1 bonus to all Piloting checks along with certain Gunnery checks. If the machine suffers internal damage or a critical hit, they must make a BOD/WIL check or suffer 2D6 points of damage plus their margin of error. Gamemasters who wish to account for VDNI's madness effect may grant warriors 1 level of any Madness Trait per two full years of implantation.

extract.name: Booby Trap
extract.tonnage: 10% of unit's weight (rounded up to nearest half ton for units over 5 tons or nearest kilogram for units under 5 tons)
extract.notes: A Booby Trap weighs 10% of a unit's weight (rounded up to the nearest half ton for every unit over 5 tons or nearest kilogram for units under 5 tons) for every unit except mobile structures. A unit can only carry one Booby Trap, and it must be carried in the same location as the unit's engine (center torso, vehicle body, fighter aft, etc.). A Mobile Structure must devote two tons per level of structure to a Booby Trap. The Booby Trap can be activated during the Weapons Attack or Physical Attack phase; It activates immediately and completely destroys the unit carrying it. When activated the Booby Trap inflicts damage in a manner similar to an artillery strike to ground units. Any unit in the same hex as the booby-trapped unit suffers damage equal to the unit's engine rating. If a unit lacks an engine rating, multiply cruise/safe MP by tonnage and use that value (maximum 500). Mobile structures use the formula MP times number of hexes times number of levels (maximum 500). Units that are one hex away from the exploding booby trap receive damage equal to one half the exploding unit's engine rating. Units two hexes away take damage equal to one quarter of the exploding unit's engine rating, while units three hexes away sustain damage equal to one-eighth of the unit's engine rating. Units four hexes or more away from the booby trap take no damage. Aerospace units that detonate a Booby Trap in space inflict no damage on nearby units. Airborne units that activate a booby trap inflict damage on other airborne units that are in the same hex on the Low Altitude map. The other airborne unit must make a control roll/piloting skill roll when the booby trap activates. Should that roll fail, the airborne unit takes damage equal to one eighth the engine rating of the booby-trapped unit. Ground units that are within three levels and three hexes of an exploding airborne unit check for damage as an airborne unit. Any non-water hex on a planet with an atmosphere will have a fire in the hex directly underneath the Booby Trap. A critical hit to the Booby Trap will not detonate it, but instead disable the arming system, rendering the Booby Trap unusable.

extract.name: Cargo
extract.notes: Apocryphal scenario published in Wunderwelten issue #23 (October 1994), pp. 80–88. The scenario 'Cargo Queen' features a JumpShip named 'Cargo Queen' (Individual Invader-class) that is captured by spaceborne infantry from Camerons Legion. The story mentions security systems, nonmagnetic floors with Velcro coating, and foam guns used to seal pressure leaks during the boarding operation.

extract.name: Liquid Storage
extract.notes: It should be noted there have been two official [[errata]] updates since the publication of the original ''TechManual''. Errata changes done to the transport bay varies between the second update and third. Notable changes the inclusion of additional types of battle armor bays per size and tech origins (Clan and Inner Sphere) which varies in how many troopers the bay holds.

extract.name: Chaff Pod
extract.notes: Originally developed by the Lyran Alliance in 3066, entered wider service in 3069. Single-use item. Weighs one ton and takes up the same amount of space as a medium laser. Activated at the end of the mounting unit's Movement Phase. Fills the hex with obscurants that act as light smoke and are two levels high. LRM and SRM attacks are affected as though attacked by an anti-missile system. Rocket launchers and MRM salvos are not affected. Generates a one-hex ECM bubble around the unit. Effects last through the Weapon Attack and Physical Attack phase of the turn.

title: Communications Equipment

extract.name: Communications Equipment
extract.notes: Communications Equipment is always assumed to be active in gameplay so long as it is not hit or destroyed, the unit's sensors and cockpit are undamaged, and the engine is running. A unit with 3 to 6 tons of Communications Equipment grants a +1 Initiative bonus to their side, while a unit with 7 or more tons grants a +2 bonus. This bonus is lost if the unit takes a Commander Hit critical hit, or if it was hit and expended MP in the previous turn. Units with a minimum of 4 tons of Communications Equipment may determine if there are any Satellites within range and attempt an uplink. Friendly satellites may be uplinked automatically, while neutral and hostile satellites must be hacked into to gain their benefits. Any unit mounting 3 to 6 tons of Communications Equipment can generate an ECCM field the same size as that generated by an Inner Sphere Guardian ECM, though only equal in strength to half its weight. A unit with 7 or more tons can do so equal to 1 ECM suite. However, operating Communications Equipment in this way means all other bonus modifiers are lost. Using Double-Blind Rules, if a unit mounts 3 to 6 tons of Communications Equipment, each unit on its side can receive a bonus in using sensors to detect the enemy, while a unit mounting seven or more gives a larger bonus.

extract.name: Collapsible Command Module
extract.notes: Introduced in 2710 by the Terran Hegemony, the Collapsible Command Module is a mobile headquarters which can be carried and deployed from the torso of a BattleMech, most famously the command variant of the Cyclops. The command bunker can be detached from the 'Mech and set up in 15 minutes, allowing for full command and coordination of an entire regiment.

extract.name: HarJel II

rules_refs.book: Masters and Minions: The StarCorps Dossiers
Masters and Minions: The StarCorps Dossiers

extract.notes: HarJel is used in several capacities: As a component of Elemental armor it is used to absorb shock, seal breaches in the armor and control bleeding should the Elemental warrior be wounded; As hull sealant on Clan spaceships; The BattleMech HarJel System, later refined to HarJel II and HarJel III.

extract.name: HarJel III

rules_refs.book: Masters and Minions: The StarCorps Dossiers
Masters and Minions: The StarCorps Dossiers

extract.notes: HarJel III is a refined version of the HarJel system used as hull sealant on Clan spaceships and as a component in Elemental armor to absorb shock, seal breaches, and control bleeding. It was developed by Clan Sea Fox (later Clan Diamond Shark) and later produced jointly by Clan Cloud Cobra and Clan Stone Lion after the Sharks left the Clan Homeworlds. After the Great Refusal, synthetic HarJel was developed by Clan Hell's Horses and Clan Ice Hellion, threatening the monopoly. Clan Diamond Shark later discovered an organic compound similar to HarJel on Jonah's Reach in the Twycross system and acquired Itabaiana from Clan Nova Cat in 3065 which included two percent of HarJel production from Twycross.

extract.name: Paramedic Equipment
extract.notes: May be mounted on any unit in 0.25 Ton allocations in accordance with standard construction rules except ProtoMechs. The Availability Rating is C-C-C.

extract.name: RISC Viral Jammer
extract.notes: Published as the 2025 April Fools product, the thirty-first entry in CGL's PDF exclusive mini-Technical Readout or TROlet series, 'Technical Readout: RISC' covers designs using technology developed by the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat and the Rhodes Foundry. Although essentially an April Fools gag publication, 'Technical Readout: RISC' has been officially confirmed to be fully canon.

extract.name: RISC Laser Pulse Module
extract.notes: Only prototypes ever made it into the field. These only offered a small improvement to standard lasers at the cost of increased heat and possible catastrophic failure of the module and the laser it was attached to. A Laser Pulse Module can be attached to an ER or standard laser of any size, as long as it has an Inner Sphere technology base. It can be used by any combat unit other than battle armor and conventional infantry. A Laser Pulse Module can only modify one single laser, and a laser can only have one LPM attached to it. The LPM must be placed in the same location as the laser it modifies; this can affect turret weight of vehicles and it does affect the size of Targeting Computers. In combat, the LPM-modified laser can operate in its standard mode or operate as a pulse laser. Standard mode uses the laser's standard range, damage, and attack modifiers. When the LPM is activated to use pulse mode, the standard range and damage values apply, but the laser gets a -2 to hit modifier and +2 heat, regardless of laser size. If a modified laser rolls an unmodified 2 on the to-hit roll or the LPM is damaged by a critical hit, the LPM will catastrophically fail. This inflicts a 2 point ammunition explosion on the location mounting the LPM. Instead of rolling for critical hits normally, the unit suffers a single automatic critical hit to the first undamaged slot of the laser that uses the LPM. If the laser attached to the LPM is damaged via critical hit before the LPM is damaged, the LPM is rendered inert as well. An inert LPM does not explode on a critical hit. Lasers with LPMs can use Targeting Computers, but when firing in pulse mode they cannot use the Targeting Computer for an aimed shot.

extract.name: Super-Cooled Myomer
extract.notes: Not compatible with any other type of myomer or myomer enhancements. Any 'Mech mounting this system is automatically made Difficult to Maintain. When SCM receives a critical hit, the defender must mark off a heat sink of their choice, to reflect damage to the overall cooling system of the 'Mech.

extract.name: Improved Sensors
extract.notes: Improved sensors weigh 65kg and are limited to one per battle armor. A unit equipped with improved sensors provides a -1 bonus to any search and rescue success rolls.

extract.name: LAM Bomb Bay
extract.notes: The CSV 'Glamorgan' was reported to be operating independently of the ComStar fleet, on detached duty alongside its sister ship the Rosslare, and operating out of the Columbus Deep Periphery station in support of Explorer Corps operations.

rules_refs.book: Masters and Minions: The StarCorps Dossiers

extract.notes: The CSV 'Glamorgan' is occasionally misspelled as 'G'a'lamorgan', but it has been confirmed by Chris Hartford that the correct spelling of the name is indeed "Glamorgan." (As officially confirmed in this reply by Chris Hartford in the "Ask the Writers" section on the BattleTech Forum: "They should be Rosslare (named for the Irish port) and Glamorgan (named for the Welsh county).")

extract.name: QuadVee Wheels
extract.notes: For the miniatures set published by German licensee FanPro in 1992, see ...Mechs!

extract.name: BattleMech Turret
extract.notes: A BattleMech turret is like a vehicle turret such that weapons mounted to it have enhanced firing arcs. Unlike vehicle turrets, the BattleMech turret is not an independent hit location of the 'Mech and cannot be armored separately, nor does it have an internal structure value. The turret is counted as a part of the location in which it is mounted. One critical slot must be allocated for the rotation mechanism of the turret. If this slot receives a critical hit, the turret is jammed in its current facing. Turret-mounted weapons and equipment receive critical hits normally.

extract.name: Ram Plate
extract.notes: Appeared during the Hanseatic Crusade in 3140. Notably featured on the Rhino Quad 'Mech. Increases 'mech's damage during a charge by 50% and reduces damage received during a charge by 50%. Can only be mounted on a Quad 'mech with Reinforced Structure. Virtually zero adoption outside of initial use on the Rhino due to mounting restrictions and risks associated with full-body charges.

extract.name: Artemis V Fire Control System
extract.notes: Developed by Clan Goliath Scorpion scientists in 3061. An improved, next generation version of the ubiquitous Artemis IV FCS. Attached to each standard LRM and SRM on the equipped 'Mech to improve the accuracy of their fired missiles.

extract.name: Apollo Fire Control System
extract.notes: Functioning much like a Targeting Computer, the fire control system makes it more likely that the launcher will achieve a missile lock, though the dumb-fire MRMs are still more prone to miss the target than other missiles.
